issue.title: Escalation banner stays visible after the HITL issue is resolved
issue.body:
## Summary

The dashboard's red escalation banner keeps reading "1 issue awaiting human
input" after the underlying HITL issue has been resolved. It only clears on a
hard page reload, so operators watching the board believe the queue is blocked
when it is not.

## Reproduction

1. Label an open issue `hydraflow-hitl` and wait for `HITLRunner` to post its
   question comment (about 30s on the sandbox fleet).
2. Open the run dashboard at `/dashboard`. The escalation banner appears with a
   link to the issue.
3. Answer the question in the issue thread and remove the `hydraflow-hitl`
   label so the issue leaves the escalation set.
4. Watch the banner for two minutes without reloading.

## Expected

The banner disappears within one poll interval (5s) of the issue leaving the
escalation set, and `GET /api/escalations` no longer lists it.

## Observed

`GET /api/escalations` correctly returns `[]` once the label is removed, so the
API side is fine. The front end keeps rendering the last non-empty payload
because `renderEscalations()` early-returns when the list is empty instead of
clearing the container. Separately, `HITLRunner.reconcile_escalations()` only
ever adds to `self._escalations` — resolved issues stay in the in-memory set
until the process restarts, so a fleet restart is currently the only way to get
a correct count from a long-running orchestrator.

## Affected

- `src/hitl_runner.py` — `reconcile_escalations()` never removes entries
- `web/api.py` — `/api/escalations` returns 204 with no body when the set is
  empty, which the front end treats as "no update"
- `web/static/js/dashboard.js` — `renderEscalations()` early-return
- No regression coverage in `tests/test_hitl_runner.py`

## Notes

Reported twice in one week by the on-call rotation. Second report included a
screenshot of a banner citing issue #4610, which had been closed for six days.

args.plan_text:
# Implementation plan — issue #4821

## Task 1 — Make `reconcile_escalations()` two-way

`HITLRunner.reconcile_escalations(open_hitl)` currently loops over the live
label set and inserts anything missing from `self._escalations`. Change it to
diff in both directions: insert `live - current`, delete `current - live`.
Publish a single `ESCALATION_RESOLVED` event carrying the sorted list of
removed issue numbers so the event bus (and the dashboard SSE feed) sees one
message per poll rather than one per issue.

Return `sorted(self._escalations)` instead of `list(...)` so the ordering the
dashboard renders is stable between polls.

## Task 2 — Always return a JSON body from `/api/escalations`

The handler returns `Response(status_code=204)` on an empty set. Return
`JSONResponse([])` with status 200 instead. 204 is the reason the front end
cannot distinguish "nothing changed" from "nothing left".

## Task 3 — Clear the container in `renderEscalations()`

Delete the `if (!items.length) return;` guard. When the payload is empty,
empty the container and set `hidden` on the banner element. When it is
non-empty, render as before.

## Task 4 — Regression coverage

Add `tests/test_hitl_runner.py::test_reconcile_drops_resolved_escalations`:
seed two escalations, reconcile with only one still labelled, assert the other
is gone from the set, that it appears in the returned `ESCALATION_RESOLVED`
payload, and that a second reconcile with the same input publishes nothing
(idempotence). Add `tests/test_web_api.py::test_escalations_empty_returns_200`.

## Out of scope

Escalation history persistence across restarts. The in-memory set is
authoritative for the current process by design (ADR-0029); this plan only
fixes the removal path.

src/hitl_runner.py               | 38 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++-----
 web/api.py                       |  6 ++++--
 web/static/js/dashboard.js       | 14 ++++++++++---
 tests/test_hitl_runner.py        | 38 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 tests/test_web_api.py            |  9 +++++++++
 5 files changed, 92 insertions(+), 13 deletions(-)

Key changes:
- src/hitl_runner.py: reconcile_escalations() now diffs the live label set in
  both directions and deletes resolved entries; publishes one
  ESCALATION_RESOLVED event per poll carrying the sorted removed issue numbers.
- web/api.py: GET /api/escalations returns JSONResponse([]) with status 200 on
  an empty set instead of a bare 204.
- web/static/js/dashboard.js: renderEscalations() clears the list container and
  hides the banner on an empty payload; toggles aria-live with visibility.
- tests: two new HITLRunner regression tests (removal + idempotence) and one
  web API test asserting the 200/empty-array contract.
args.precheck_context:
PRECHECK_RISK: medium
PRECHECK_CONFIDENCE: 0.72
PRECHECK_ESCALATE: no
PRECHECK_SUMMARY: Backend removal path and API status-code change are directly evidenced in the diff; the front-end banner-clearing criterion and the 5s timing claim are only partly checkable from a static diff.

Notes from the low-tier pass:
- `reconcile_escalations()` now deletes resolved keys and publishes one
  ESCALATION_RESOLVED event, so AC-1 and AC-2 have direct diff evidence.
- `/api/escalations` returns JSONResponse([], status_code=200); the 204 branch
  is gone, so AC-3 has direct evidence.
- AC-4 asserts observable timing ("within one 5s poll interval"). The diff
  shows the container clear and the `hidden` toggle but nothing about the poll
  cadence, so timing is unverifiable from the diff alone.
- AC-5 requires that the new test fails pre-fix. The diff shows the test but
  not a red run, so treat the fail-first half as unproven unless the PR body
  records it.
